article_content: A Virginia court ruled fingerprints aren't protected under the Fifth Amendment, allowing authorities easier access to devices like iPhones secured by Touch ID. Judge Steven C. Fucci's decision holds that defendants can't be forced to disclose passcodes or PINs, but must provide fingerprints to unlock biometric-enabled devices. The Fifth Amendment's self-incrimination clause bars compelling memorized information, but doesn't apply to physical characteristics like fingerprints. This ruling stems from a case involving David Baust, charged with strangling his girlfriend. Prosecutors sought to compel him to unlock his phone, believed to contain evidence of the attack. While he couldn't be forced to reveal a passcode, authorities could legally demand fingerprint access. Prosecutors are considering an appeal.

article_content: Scott Campbell, a 49-year-old Florida man, was convicted of first-degree grand theft for orchestrating a decade-long scheme that defrauded over 30 women of more than $1 million. Operating under the guise of a fictional record label, BDO Records, Campbell lured targets through dating and social media platforms, promising opportunities in a talent contest titled 'Give Me a Chance,' marketed as rivaling shows like American Idol. Prosecutors revealed the funds were funneled into his personal lifestyle rather than business ventures. Victims described Campbell as a manipulative 'vampire' who preyed on women with low self-esteem, extracting financial and emotional resources until they were depleted. Among the victims was Kim Serravalle, who mortgaged her home to provide $70,000, while another lost $300,000. Ex-girlfriend Jeannie Thompson recounted his exploitative tactics, stating he 'sucked everything out of you.' Campbell faces up to 30 years in prison upon sentencing in February.

article_content: Reuters Apparel exports are expected to reach USD 40 billion by 2030 due to initiatives such as exploring new markets and fostering strategic partnerships, the Apparel Export Promotion Council of India (AEPC) said on Friday. AEPC Chairman Naren Goenka stated the council will focus on innovation, expanding market reach and product diversity, practicing sustainability, and responsible business practices. 'We have set an ambitious goal of achieving apparel exports of USD 40 billion by 2030,' he said. This target, named '40 by 30,' reflects commitment to growth. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal will present export awards to garment exporters on December 9. These awards honor contributions to modernizing Indian enterprises. Exports of ready-made garments from April-September 2023-24 totaled USD 6.92 billion, a 15.3% drop from the same period last year. In FY22-23, exports reached USD 16.2 billion.
